audit.why: Melee assassin with no level-1 escape; Twilight Shroud (W) only arrives at 3+. Aatrox owns levels 1-5, Akali takes over at 6 and again on assassin items — the existing level chart already reflects that.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 phase text was a generic template that named no ultimate and no cooldown.
audit.why: Level 6 is Perfect Execution (R), a two-part dash execute on 120/90/60. She opens it from Twilight Shroud (W, 20/19/18/17/16), so World Ender (120/100/80) must be saved for her jump.
audit.corrected: Perfect Execution (R) is a two-part dash execute on 120s, and she opens it out of Twilight Shroud. Hold World Ender for her jump, then out-drain the combo rather than racing it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Key Ability Interactions described Infernal Chains (W) as a root; Riot’s text says enemies are dragged back to the centre if they do not leave the zone, and the decisive interaction for this matchup was absent.
audit.why: Twilight Shroud makes her unable to be selected by enemy spells while inside, so Infernal Chains (W) and World Ender cannot pick her out of it — The Darkin Blade (Q) is a ground slam and still lands. Shuriken Flip (E) is 16/14.5/13/11.5/10, the window to chain her.
audit.corrected: Your Q sweetspot (outer edge) is your damage and your heal — land the edge, never the inner hit, and use E mid-cast to swing the sweetspot onto her. Infernal Chains (W) drags her back to the centre if she doesn't leave the zone, so hold it until Shuriken Flip (E, 16s at rank 1) is spent, then chain her for Q2/Q3. Inside Twilight Shroud (W, 20s) your W and R cannot select her — Q is a ground slam and still lands, so keep swinging through the smoke. Save World Ender for her Perfect Execution commit.

edits.before: Ultimate interaction changes all-ins. At level 6, reassess the matchup. Aatrox gains his ultimate, but Akali's ultimate or scaling pattern may change whether you can commit.
edits.after: Perfect Execution (R) is a two-part dash execute on 120s, and she opens it out of Twilight Shroud. Hold World Ender for her jump, then out-drain the combo rather than racing it.

edits.before: Your Q sweetspot (outer edge) is your damage and your heal — land the edge, never the inner hit, and use E mid-cast to swing the sweetspot onto Akali. W (Infernal Chains) roots him if he doesn't leave the zone: use it to lock him for Q2/Q3 or to cut off his escape. He's mobile, so hold W until after he commits his dash, then chain him so he can't reset or kite your Q. Pop R (World Ender) for the heal, AD and move speed when you fully commit or to survive Perfect Execution — never burn it for a single Q.
